key_facts: UPDATED Sun Sep 13 (T+1d to Mon Sep 14 ceremony; Exa Gold Derby Sep 11 + Deadline Sep 11 + Covers Sep 11 + Guardian Sep 12/13 + Forbes Sep 13; local Sep 13 scan empty; SUBMITTED Widow's Bay 0.77->0.75 [-0.02], Hacks 0.21->0.23 [+0.02], The Bear 0.004->0.006, Abbott Elementary 0.005->0.004, Margo's Got Money Troubles 0.004 [replacing #8 Shrinking]; sum=0.994, outside=0.006): Fresh pre-ceremony coverage confirms a genuine two-horse race ahead of Monday night's 78th Primetime Emmys. While Forbes (Sep 13) and Gold Derby (live odds: Widow's Bay 67.8%, Hacks 31.1%, The Bear 0.4%, Abbott Elementary 0.2%, Margo's Got Money Troubles 0.2%, OMITB 0.2%, NWT/Shrinking <0.1%) still back Apple TV+'s 8-Creative-Arts-winner Widow's Bay (with Matthew Rhys 96.2% Lead Actor, Kate O'Flynn 75.1% Supporting Actress), Deadline's Pete Hammond (Sep 11) explicitly picked Hacks to win Comedy Series — highlighting that (1) Hacks won a record 24 noms for its final season, (2) Hacks beat Widow's Bay head-to-head in Picture Editing (only Hacks' 2nd crafts Emmy ever), (3) 7 of Widow's Bay's 8 wins are crafts and its sole above-the-line win (Betty Gilpin, Guest Actress) benefited from 5 Hacks nominees splitting the vote, and (4) Hacks pulled the exact same full-Academy upset over 11-win The Bear S2 in 2024. Covers (Sep 11) also noted Widow's Bay and Hacks 'jostling for favoritism' and Guardian (Sep 12/13) called it 'a real race'. A 60/40 blend of post-Creative Arts markets (~80/19) and Gold Derby (67.8/31.1) centers cleanly at 0.75/0.23.
